title: AngelaMos 3D
subtitle: Ollama + Whisper + OpenWakeWord + Three.js VRM — voice assistant with a body
description: Local-first voice assistant with a 3D VRM avatar. Wake word detection streams mic audio via AudioWorklet over WebSocket to OpenWakeWord running in a FastAPI backend. On trigger, records until silence detection, transcribes with faster-whisper, streams response from Ollama, synthesizes with Edge TTS, then plays back with real-time lip sync driven by Web Audio frequency analysis. The frontend is a Three.js scene — not a chat UI.
technical_details:
# Mixamo to VRM Animation Retargeting

Converts Mixamo FBX bone space to VRM normalized bone space via quaternion premultiplication against world-space rest rotations. Handles VRM 0.x coordinate flip and scales hips position by the ratio of VRM rest pose height to Mixamo rig height.

# Animation State Machine with Combo Queuing

AnimationManager runs an idle loop that waits 22s, then picks 1-2 random action animations, chains them sequentially with 0.3s crossfade, then returns to base idle. Speaking state cycles through breakdance/flair clips. Transitions cancel current schedule and flush the action queue.

# Inline AudioWorklet Wake Word Pipeline

WakeWordEngine defines and registers an AudioWorkletProcessor at runtime via a Blob URL. The processor buffers Float32 mic samples into fixed-size chunks (80ms at native sample rate), converts to Int16, and sends over a WebSocket to OpenWakeWord. Each WebSocket session gets a fresh model instance to avoid shared prediction state.

# Frequency-Driven Lip Sync

During TTS playback, an AnalyserNode reads frequency data every animation frame. Low-frequency band average (bottom 30% of bins) is scaled and clamped to drive the VRM 'aa' expression. Mouth closes immediately on playback end.

# In-Browser WAV Encoding

AudioRecorder decodes MediaRecorder output through AudioContext, then manually writes a RIFF/WAV header into an ArrayBuffer before sending to the Whisper endpoint. No external audio encoding library.
